description: The fifth collection combines the autumn 2025 run, the five-night Rollover experiment, Christmas and Valentine's specials, the early-2026 continuation and a Kids Special, while retaining the same escalating logic-first format.

s05e01.description: TEAR is built from images, RUG plus BEE becomes RUGBY and SEAL plus ANT becomes SEALANT. Later clues hide a star in COSTA RICA, LIAM inside PARLIAMENT and swap 9 with 2 before a left-right path spells BADGE.

s05e02.description: A pair-of-pictures question depends on saying the pictured names aloud, a caterpillar requires adding and subtracting its numbers and a word grid hides valid four-letter words. The final treats the digits as two-digit alphabet positions, revealing SPAIN.

s05e03.description: A deceptively destructive 60-percent puzzle gives three sentences and asks for one name that makes each contain five words beginning with the same letter. Later word and visual questions continue the pattern of instructions that matter more than general knowledge.

s05e04.description: An alternating-digit calculation turns 23055023 into paired values that sum to 5555, while a five-by-five alphabet grid produces N. The one-percent question hides mistakes in its own small print and terms, with the required count being seven.

s05e05.description: A missing cap, reversed letter pairs, colour-order logic and a cumulative sum puzzle precede a dense square-counting final. The four-by-four grid contains ordinary squares plus a smaller square inside every cell, bringing the total to forty-six.

s05e06.description: Rock-paper-scissors logic and a long sentence missing the letter G make the opening Rollover night unusually punishing. The final asks contestants to identify the missing and repeated values in a dense sequence, with nineteen providing the crucial missing answer.

s05e07.description: Cutlery orientation and a dartboard are among the visual traps before the final converts the word HEAD into the digits 8514. Reading the letters through the puzzle's number code gives the four-digit one-percent answer.

s05e08.description: A horizontal-versus-vertical puzzle, turning FRANCE into ORANGE and a dartboard challenge lead into number play. One question asks for the smallest amount that must be added to 12316 to make a palindrome, making the episode a parade of rules that only look obvious afterwards.

s05e09.description: Animal-leg counting appears late in the ladder before the one-percent puzzle encodes a congratulatory phrase. Following the letter rule reveals WELL DONE, an answer one finalist recognizes with enough confidence to commit immediately.

s05e10.description: A sun-cream reading question removes contestants who overlook what the text actually mentions, before the final converts number words into a five-digit sequence. The one-percent answer is 31459, with the N in ONE supplying the otherwise easy-to-miss second digit.

s05e11.description: Christmas Day brings reindeer ordering, festive counting and seasonal word traps before the one-percent question turns to the Twelve Days of Christmas. The concealed answer is HEN, as in the French hens, a final that proves kinder than several of the earlier Christmas puzzles.

s05e12.description: One question plays with numerals leaning left or right, while the final asks for the lowest number whose written name fits a relationship between its vowels, consonants and total letters. FIFTEEN satisfies the required seven-letter structure.

s05e13.description: Table settings test left- and right-handed assumptions, a visual clue resolves to SNAP and a rebus-like word split produces EXTR-OVER-T, or EXTROVERT. A later dice problem asks contestants to read the pictured values with rather more care than the artwork deserves.

s05e14.description: A sequence removes parts of shape names: TRIANGLE becomes ANGLE, SQUARE reduces to RE and PENTAGON to GON. Following the same rule leaves N from HEXAGON, a language puzzle disguised as a geometry sequence.

s05e15.description: The ladder leans heavily on wording and visual comparison, including an odd-one-out problem where the tempting semantic answer is not necessarily the structural one. The later questions reward counting exactly what is shown rather than importing the obvious category.

s05e16.description: Nested words and picture clues dominate the late ladder, forcing contestants to look for shorter answers hidden inside longer ones and to distinguish sound-alike clues from literal spellings. The final continues that same compression of language into a small structural rule.

s05e17.description: The Valentine's special turns couples, hearts and relationship language into pattern puzzles rather than romance trivia. Word transformations and paired visual clues build toward a final affectionate answer, SWEETHEART, reached by following the construction rather than the sentiment.

s05e18.description: A late number-word puzzle combines written numbers rather than merely adding their values. TEN, EIGHT, ONE and TWO are manipulated through their letters and order, with the closing rule producing twenty-one.

s05e19.description: The five-percent question's intended answer is BACK, a trap severe enough to remove the remaining finalists. The one-percent puzzle then converts a sequence of clock times, 12, 1, 2, 5 and 12, into letters that spell LABEL.

s05e20.description: The Kids Special gives younger contestants the same escalating logic format, including a hidden-animal puzzle and a final sentence whose structure is palindromic. The last concealed creature resolves to WORM, proving the children's edition has no intention of becoming a nursery quiz.
